# Aṭṭhakanipāta (AN 8)
**ID:** AN 8
**Section:** Aṅguttaranikāya (an)

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
It organizes teachings around thematic and numerical sets of eight dhammas across 73 suttas in the SuttaCentral division [SuttaCentral]. Notable discourses include the *Uposathasutta* (AN 8.20), treating the suspension of the monastic Observance [Lueritthikul 2015; SuttaCentral]; the *Gotamīsutta* (AN 8.51), concerning Mahāpajāpatī Gotamī's request for ordination and the eight *garudhammas* [Anālayo 2011; Anālayo 2016; SuttaCentral]; and the *Bhūmicālasutta* (AN 8.70), presenting the eight causes of earthquakes [Walshe 1987; SuttaCentral].
Curated records list parallels for all 73 suttas across early canonical corpora, including 16 in the Chinese *Madhyama-āgama*, 13 individual Chinese translations, 10 in other Pali texts, 9 in the *Ekottarika-āgama*, and 14 across *Saṃyuktāgama* collections (T 99 and T 100), in addition to Sanskrit and Tibetan Vinaya parallels for texts like the *Uposathasutta* and *Gotamīsutta* [SuttaCentral; Lueritthikul 2015; Anālayo 2011; Anālayo 2016]. DharmaNexus records over 60,000 Pali-internal text-reuse matches with 629 texts, showing substantial shared phrasing with adjacent *Aṅguttaranikāya* books (AN 5, AN 4, AN 10, AN 3, AN 6, AN 7), the Vinaya Khandhakas (Kd 6 and Kd 19), the *Mahāparinibbāna Sutta* (DN 16), and the Udāna (Ud 5.5) [DharmaNexus]. Furthermore, DharmaNexus computes cross-language alignments between AN 8 discourses and the *Divyāvadāna*, the Sanskrit *Saṅghabhedavastu*, the Tibetan *Vinayavastu* and *Abhidharmakośaṭīkopayikā*, and Chinese Āgama collections [DharmaNexus].
